purpose: Retains the evidence for storing the retired WSL retrieval lock as package-lock.json.frozen. No dependency scanner reads that name, so the lock leaves the discovery that raised Dependabot alert 17 and Scorecard code-scanning alert 19, and the dedicated OSV-Scanner grant, due to expire on 2026-10-17, is deleted with its scan group.
fixed_means: If GitHub reports alert 17 or alert 19 as fixed after this change merges, fixed means the lock was removed from name-based discovery. Nothing was patched: the archived bytes still pin braces 3.0.3, which GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (CVE-2026-93687, high) affects and for which no patched release exists.
authorization: The coordinating session assigned this change on 2026-10-04. It carries out the 2026-10-03 convergence decision to rename both frozen npm locks to .frozen and stop scanning them in a follow-up pull request (docs/decisions/2026-09-22-github-automation-closure.md, alert-16 note, and the indirect_routes field of evidence/receipts/dependabot-alert-16-dismissal-20261003.json), for the WSL lock only, as PR-1 and option (b) of the 2026-10-04 GitHub-automation audit. It writes nothing outward except its pull request and dismisses no alert. Option (a), dismissing alert 17, would need the user's explicit authorization naming alert 17.
evidence_class: Native runs of the pinned OSV-Scanner v2.6.0 binary on scratch copies (local, sanitized output retained); one read-only GitHub REST API GET of alert 17; local integration tests and local fault injection for the guard; source review of the cited documentation. No CI run, no live dependency-graph or code-scanning transition and no new-host acceptance is claimed here.

The security-scan.yml preflight still runs tests.test_wsl_retrieval.RetiredRunnerTests, whose audit.py run now includes the discovery guard.

The macOS variant (alert 16's artifact), its OSV config and its tripwire's scope are unchanged; tests/test_frozen_macos_variant_no_use.py re-pins only the edited workflow assignment line, its copy in the coverage test and the edited dependabot.yml comment line.

guard_mutation_checks.summary: M0, the unmutated guard, passes all 11 scenarios. Each of the eight code mutants M1-M8 (archive digest, assessment digest, disk names, npm-shrinkwrap.json, recursive walk, letter case, archive tracking, index names) fails its designated scenario with one failure and no error. N1, a message-only edit, survives as a negative control. LockDiscoveryGuardTests.test_each_requirement_is_enforced_by_a_scenario re-runs M1-M8 in every unittest run.

post_merge_readback.expected: Alert 17 fixed once the default branch's dependency graph no longer lists the lock; alert 19 fixed after the next Scorecard analysis of main no longer reports the advisory.
post_merge_readback.stop_condition: If alert 17 is still open after the merge, stop and bring option (a) to the user; it needs the user's explicit authorization naming alert 17. Never dismiss alert 19.

limitations: The fixed state is expected from GitHub's documented meaning of fixed_at, not observed: no live dependency-graph or code-scanning transition was seen before merge. The coordinator's read-back is that evidence, and the stop condition governs a different outcome.
Alert 19 can clear only after a Scorecard run on main, and only if code scanning closes a location-less alert that a new analysis stops reporting; neither was observed.

The OSV controls are native runs on scratch copies with sanitized paths, not the CI workflow. The workflow's two-group routing is covered by recording-double tests, which are synthetic, and by the pull request's CI run.

The guard covers name-based discovery in this partition only. It does not prove that nothing restores or installs the archived bytes; the directory offers no supported route, and the 2026-10-03 devEngines guard covers supported npm entry points only.
braces 3.0.3 remains in the archived bytes. Active QMD 2.8.3 resolves braces 3.0.3 without a tracked lock; that reachability review is a separate item and is not addressed here.
audit.py fails closed outside a Git checkout, so it cannot pass on an exported tree without Git metadata.
overturn: Restore a reviewed scan of this lock if GitHub's dependency graph, OSV-Scanner or Scorecard starts reading .frozen names, or if the lock's bytes change or an install or replay route for it returns (then it takes its npm name and the normal scan, or a new dated decision, as the 2026-09-25 decision's overturn says). If alert 17 stays open after the merge, apply the stop condition.
